record.context_brief: Cox-process extensions of the MMPP conjectures
record.original_question: Do analogues of the two MMPP conjectures extend to general Cox processes under suitable regularity conditions? More specifically, for Cox processes satisfying appropriate regularity assumptions, must the squared coefficient of variation of the event-stationary inter-event time be at least 1 and must the time-stationary first inter-event time stochastically dominate the event-stationary first inter-event time?

evidence.quote: In fact, since any Cox process can be approximated by an MMPP, we believe that versions of conjectures 1 and 2 also hold for Cox processes under suitable regularity conditions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N = (N_t)_{t \geq 0}$ be a Cox process (doubly stochastic Poisson process) on the real line, that is, a point process which, conditional on a non-negative stochastic intensity process $\Lambda = (\Lambda_t)_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$, is an inhomogeneous Poisson process with intensity $\Lambda$. Assume that $\Lambda$ is stationary and ergodic with finite, strictly positive mean rate $\lambda = \mathbb{E}[\Lambda_0] \in (0,\infty)$, together with whatever further regularity conditions (e.g.\ integrability and mixing) are needed to make the constructions below well defined.

Associated to $N$ are two canonical inter-event-time distributions:

(a) The time-stationary first inter-event time $T^\ast$: under the time-stationary (Palm-with-respect-to-Lebesgue) law, $T^\ast$ is the waiting time from an arbitrary deterministic time origin until the next event of $N$.

(b) The event-stationary inter-event time $T$: under the Palm distribution of $N$ (the law of the process as seen from a typical event), $T$ is the time between two consecutive events.

Prove or disprove the following two statements for every such Cox process satisfying the regularity assumptions:

1. The squared coefficient of variation of $T$ satisfies
$$\mathrm{CV}^2(T) \;=\; \frac{\mathrm{Var}(T)}{(\mathbb{E}[T])^2} \;\geq\; 1.$$

2. The time-stationary first inter-event time stochastically dominates the event-stationary inter-event time, i.e.
$$\mathbb{P}(T^\ast > t) \;\geq\; \mathbb{P}(T > t) \qquad \text{for all } t \geq 0.$$
artifact.category_tag: Cox processes and point process inter-event times
artifact.status_search_result: The two statements are conjectured (not proven) for general MMPPs; the question of whether analogous statements hold for general Cox processes under regularity conditions is posed as an open extension. A 2018 preprint establishes the squared coefficient of variation inequality for MMPPs in some settings, but no general proof for Cox processes appears in the literature; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Squared Coefficient of Variation for MMPP is Greater than Unity
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses the squared coefficient of variation conjecture for MMPP, the special case underlying the broader Cox-process question.
status_evidence.claim: The MMPP version of the SCV conjecture is studied; the Cox-process generalization is not established.

status_evidence.title: Stationary Markovian Arrival Processes, Results and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Conjectures on event-stationary SCV ≥ 1 and stochastic domination of time-stationary by event-stationary inter-arrival are stated as open, with conjectured extension to Cox processes.
status_evidence.claim: The Cox-process analogues are stated as open conjectures.
